issues.legal_issue: A person in possession who claims an independent right in immovable property may resist an attempted dispossession in execution, and the executing court must adjudicate the objection rather than dismiss it as non-maintainable.
material_facts: The objectors claimed that they had acquired the land from pattadars and that their rights arose before the partition suit and its decree.
They claimed to be in possession and to have built houses on the land, and resisted delivery of possession under the decree to its assignees.
The lower courts dismissed their objections as non-maintainable without deciding their claims, reasoning that they claimed through persons who were parties to the suit.
issues.conclusion: The dismissal as non-maintainable was unsustainable. The orders were set aside and the objections were remitted for fresh consideration; the Court did not decide the objectors’ title on the merits.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 21 Rules 97 and 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the executing court must determine questions relevant to an objection to execution, including questions of right, title or interest, rather than requiring a separate suit. A person claiming an independent right may object before being dispossessed; Rule 99 concerns an application after dispossession. The Court relied on Silverline Forum Pvt. Ltd. v. Rajiv Trust, (1998) 3 SCC 723; Shreenath v. Rajesh, (1998) 4 SCC 543; and Anwarbi v. Pramod D.A. Joshi, (2000) 10 SCC 405. It also referred to Order 21 Rules 35, 36, 99 and 103, and to Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act in discussing transferees pendente lite.

rule.if: execution_for_possession and objector_in_possession and claims_independent_property_right and resists_attempted_dispossession

predicates.execution_for_possession: The proceeding seeks delivery of possession of immovable property under a decree.
predicates.objector_in_possession: A person other than the judgment-debtor claims to be in possession of the property.
predicates.claims_independent_property_right: The objector asserts a right in the property independent of the judgment-debtor’s right under the decree.
predicates.resists_attempted_dispossession: The objector opposes an attempt to dispossess them in execution of the decree.
predicates.executing_court_must_adjudicate_objectio: The executing court determines the objection and relevant questions of right, title or interest instead of dismissing it as non-maintainable.

issues.definition: When a person in possession asserts an independent property right and resists attempted dispossession in execution of a possession decree, the executing court must adjudicate the objection.
